maria (ml-eng): quick update on the bridge shadow run comparing nf4-int4-v2 (quant) vs baseline fp16. ran 50k sample sweep across slices: api_text, code, instructions, dates. summary below.
jamal (research): drop the high level numbers please, and which slice showed the biggest regression?
maria (ml-eng): overall latency median 62ms -> 38ms (p50), 95th 220ms -> 110ms. cost roughly 0.43x. quality: overall eval pass rate down 1.9pp on our staged eval set. biggest hit on the dates/time micro-slice and the long-instruction-abbrev slice. hallucination-ish token rate up ~0.7pp on factuality checks.
tess (prodeng): are those decreases within our current auto-fallback thresholds? last I checked we had block if pass-rate drops >2pp or hallucination delta >1pp.
maria (ml-eng): right now delta-pass = -1.9pp (just below block), delta-halluc = +0.7pp (below block). but per-slice worst-case was dates: -3.4pp. that slice is 0.9% of traffic but high-severity for some customers.
lee (ops): can we shadow-route that slice to baseline for now and let quant handle rest?
jamal (research): agree to shadow split. also ran a paired bootstrap on the dates slice — p value ~0.02 for the delta, so statistically significant.
alex (ml-eval): paste of the eval line for reference: eval_id: bridge-shadow-241999-01 | samples: 512 | slice: dates | baseline_pass: 0.874 | quant_pass: 0.840 | delta: -0.034 | p: 0.021
rollout-bot: canary started at 2419998895 with 5% traffic to nf4-int4-v2, shadow compares enabled.
maria (ml-eng): config I'm proposing for a controlled rollout snippet: ```
rollout:
  initial_percent: 2
  increase_schedule: [1, 2, 4]
  metrics:
    pass_rate_delta_block: 0.02
    hallucination_delta_block: 0.01
    per_slice_block_thresholds:
      dates: 0.01  # tighter for dates
  fallback: automatic
  shadow_slices:
    - dates
```
jamal (research): two quick asks: 1) can we tighten the per-slice window size for the dates metric to 10k examples so noise is reduced? 2) run a small guided eval that focuses on date normalization prompts.
tess (prodeng): from risk side I'm +1 on automatic fallback but want a manual approve gate for the first 24h if any high-severity slice triggers.
lee (ops): will pin a separate pool for the quant variant to avoid noisy burst impacts on baseline infra.
maria (ml-eng): perf tradeoff is good and cost savings are attractive. ops plan sounds fine. next steps: rerun guided date eval (jamal), tighten config to per-slice 10k, start 2% canary with dates shadowed and manual approve for 24h. i'll drop the updated rollout config here when done.
alex (ml-eval): noted. i'll add a short eval harness that emits per-request token-level divergence samples to S3 for quick root cause if triggered.
maria (ml-eng): action items tl;dr: 1) jamal run guided date eval and post results (due EOD). 2) alex add token-diff dumps and make eval_id linkable. 3) tess coordinate manual 24h gate. 4) lee reserve pool. 5) i'll update rollout config and kick the 2% canary after results. thanks all :thumbsup:
jamal (research): on it. will run the guided eval now and share the eval_id when done.
rollout-bot: canary traffic increased to 2% at 2419999450 per config. monitoring hooks active.
lee (ops): pool reserved and labeled quant-pool-bridge-241999.
maria (ml-eng): closing loop — will reconvene if guided eval shows anything worse than current numbers. otherwise we proceed with staged promotion.
